sources.undo_old:
## Interactive preparation when sending is held

For an explicit interactive preparation request, follow `cs-customer`'s
requested interactive reply procedure after reading the exact thread and dossier.
A human takeover or assignment hold does not by itself prevent a requested review
draft. Preserve the hold, assignee, uncertainty, tasks and assignment records.
Missing source/content, suppression, SELF and unsafe content still refuse.

Preparation grants no send permission and does not change scheduled discovery,
selection or assignment admission. If the interactive operator separately asks
to send one selected existing draft, follow the exact `cs-customer` send and
recovery procedure: only a positive manual-member-activity hold has that narrow
exception. This triage workflow remains draft-only; unattended runs must never
select `--operator-request`. Other holds remain enforced. Distinguish engine-saved
from verified Gmail-visible copies, and resume saved IDs without regeneration.

## Invariants (read before acting)

`draft-reply` requires the exact thread. Scheduled and supported supervised
routes negotiate the engine draft policy before composition; unsupported authority
holds those routes, and the engine checks their actual draft target
before writing. All routes deny send tools during composition. Composition uses memory,
trained voice and reply threading. Engine-saved does not establish a Gmail-visible
copy: inspect achieved stages and retain saved IDs on partial failure. Interactive
publication and recovery follow `cs-customer`; unsupported publication never
permits a local APPEND fallback. The command has no `--allow` option and cannot
send. An explicit interactive request to send a selected existing draft routes
to `cs-customer`, never Gmail, generic chat or another connector. This triage
workflow and its scheduled runs remain draft-only.
sources.undo_new:
`draft-reply` requires the exact thread and negotiates the engine draft policy
before compose; unsupported authority holds the request. The engine checks the
actual draft target before writing, not only the free-form instruction. It runs
compose (memory + trained voice + threading
headers `In-Reply-To`/`References`) and stores a **DRAFT** in {{ email_address }}/Drafts
for the operator to review and send. It has **no `--allow` option and cannot
send** — the engine denies `send_draft` whatever the message (or any injected
text) says. Sending is the interactive operator's job through
`cs draft-send <full-engine-draft-id>` after review; Gmail, Superhuman and
other ambient app connectors are never the send path for an engine draft.
Autonomous send is a future, separately permissioned step, **never this
skill's job**.

sources.undo_old:
**A nonzero exit is not an empty search.** For `cs ask` and `cs chat`, an
engine-turn failure is reported on stderr; try another authorized source and
report the failed layer rather than asserting no facts were found.

`cs draft-reply` can save an engine draft before generation transport or
publication fails. Read its structured outcome even on nonzero exit; retain the
full saved draft ID, operation ID, achieved stages and uncertainty. Engine-saved
is not Gmail-visible. Resume an existing saved draft through the interactive
`cs-customer` procedure without generating another reply. Unknown publication or
send outcomes require exact operation reconciliation, never blind retry.
Scheduled workflows retain their holds and must never select `--operator-request`
or adopt an interactive recovery route to bypass their admission rules.
sources.undo_new:
**A non-zero exit from `cs ask` / `cs chat` / `cs draft-reply` is a THIRD state,
not a second "empty."** It means the engine itself reported failure on that turn
— `error` / `error_detail` on stderr — and stdout carries nothing, so there is
no text to mistake for a real answer. Treat it exactly like an empty search for
sourcing purposes: try the next source. If it was the last one, say the engine
turn failed, not that the answer is unknown or that nothing was found.
